name: IL-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+34 partisan lean makes a Republican win implausible
Ford's fundraising edge: $816k raised versus Koppie's $58k and $42 on hand
Polymarket prices the Democratic side near 97 percent
Open seat and no general-election polling add mild uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's 34-point Democratic lean, Ford's dominant fundraising position, and market pricing near 97 percent all point the same direction; even without polls, a Republican upset would require a historic collapse.
model.watch: Only a major scandal, ballot issue, or turnout anomaly involving Ford would put this seat in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Danny Davis (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Illinois's 7th District, centered on Chicago's West Side, carries a partisan lean of about 34 points Democratic, and longtime Representative Danny Davis is retiring. Democrat La Shawn Ford enters the general election as the clear favorite over Republican Chad Koppie, whose campaign shows minimal resources.

Ford has raised more than $800,000 to Koppie's roughly $58,000, and Koppie reported just $42 on hand. Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97 percent, and no general-election polls exist to suggest otherwise. The heavy outside spending recorded against Ford likely reflects the contested primary rather than general-election vulnerability. With fundamentals this lopsided, the seat remains safely Democratic despite the open-seat transition.
